ai.description: This slender frog reaches 8 cm. It is bright green with a distinct white or yellow dorsolateral fold and white upper lip stripe. The skin is smooth, and the toes have large, flattened discs.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Hylarana erythraea* is best distinguished by the prominent, broad, creamy-white dorsolateral folds that extend clearly from behind the eye to the groin.
ai.habitat: *Hylarana erythraea* inhabits lowland marshes, ponds, and rice paddies, typically found in dense vegetation near permanent water bodies up to 1,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Common Green Frog is primarily nocturnal, often foraging for insects along the edges of ponds and marshes under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hylarana erythraea* is an oviparous breeder that lays large clutches of 1,000–2,000 eggs in floating foam masses, typically during the monsoon season (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hylarana erythraea* is found in Northeast India, primarily within the Brahmaputra valley and surrounding foothills, typically inhabiting low-elevation wetlands.
ai.callDescription: The Common Green Frog emits a series of sharp, rhythmic "chuck-chuck" notes. These high-pitched calls are frequently heard near ponds and marshes in Southeast Asia.
